clauses: Cards and health setup
Who places where and in what order
Legal sidekick spaces, including a multizone hero space
When Alice chooses initial size
Who takes the first turn
answers.answer: The attached setup steps and fighter reference resolve the requested setup details.

evidence.text: | Alice | 13 | Melee | 2 | Jabberwock: 8, melee |
| King Arthur | 18 | Melee | 2 | Merlin: 7, ranged |
| Medusa | 16 | Ranged | 3 | 3 Harpies: 1 each, melee |
| Sinbad | 15 | Melee | 2 | Porter: 6, melee |
1. Choose a battlefield and place it on the table. Each player chooses a hero and takes that hero’s components.
2. Set the hero’s and sidekick’s dials to the starting health above; undialed sidekicks have 1 health each.
3. Each player shuffles their **30 action cards into one separate face-down deck**, then draws **5 cards**.

4. The **younger player** places their hero on starting space **1**, then their sidekick(s) in **separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero**. If the hero’s space belongs to several zones, use any of those zones. Make beginning-of-game decisions when placing that player’s fighters. **Alice’s controller**, whether younger or older, chooses **BIG or SMALL when placing Alice** and displays her size token.
5. The **older player** places their hero on starting space **2**, then places sidekicks under the same rules.
6. The younger player takes the first turn.

clauses: Required turn actions
Whether actions may be repeated or skipped
When and how to enforce the 7-card limit if holding 9
answers.answer: Two actions are mandatory; repetition is allowed, skipping is not. If holding 9 at turn end, discard 2 cards to your own discard pile to reach 7.

evidence.text: At the start of Medusa’s turn, her optional special ability may resolve (see below). Then take **2 actions** from **maneuver, scheme, attack**. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice; **you cannot skip an action**.
You may hold more than 7 cards during your turn. **At the end of your turn**, discard excess cards to your own discard pile until you have **7**, then the opponent takes their turn.

clauses: Draw and movement order during ordinary maneuver
Which fighters move and their distance
Passing friendly or enemy fighters
Ending on occupied space
Whether two fighters’ movement can be interleaved
answers.answer: Draw first, then move each fighter independently up to its allowance (including zero), completing each fighter before moving another. Friendly fighters may be passed; opposing fighters block; no fighter may finish in an occupied space.

evidence.text:
1. **Draw 1 card first, mandatory.**
2. **Optionally move** each of your fighters, one at a time, up to your move value (plus applicable bonuses). Each fighter chooses its own distance, including **zero**. Choose their order, but finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.

Ordinary movement enters adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through your own friendly fighters, but **cannot finish in any occupied space**. You may **not pass through opposing fighters**. An effect that moves opposing fighters follows the same rules **from their owner’s perspective**. Apply these movement restrictions to card movement unless that card states an exception.

clauses: How maneuver movement is BOOSTed
Discarded card effect handling
Who receives added movement
Whether defeated sidekick’s unusable card can pay BOOST
answers.answer: Discard one hand card; its BOOST value is added to the movement allowance for each of your fighters and its effects are ignored. A card unusable because its fighter is defeated may still be discarded to BOOST.

evidence.text: **BOOST movement:** during a maneuver, discard **1 card from your hand** to add its printed **BOOST value** (the small circled number, not its combat value) to the movement value for this maneuver. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. For **any permitted BOOST**, add the discarded card’s BOOST value and **ignore that card’s effects**, whether the BOOST modifies movement or an attack. A card that cannot be played because its fighter is defeated **can still be discarded to BOOST**. Effects may separately permit boosting attacks; boosting is not otherwise a universal option.

clauses: Given: empty deck; mandatory draw 2; hero and sidekick survive
Whether to reshuffle or decline
Damage to each fighter
answers.answer: Do not reshuffle or decline. Each missing draw causes each of your fighters to take 2 damage, so the two missing draws cause two separate 2-damage events to each surviving fighter.

evidence.text:
- Drawing cards, whether from maneuver or an effect, is **mandatory unless explicitly optional**.
- With an empty deck, your fighters are **exhausted**. Each time you must draw a card you cannot draw, **each of your fighters immediately takes 2 damage instead**. Do **not reshuffle** your discard pile. A mandatory draw of 2 with an empty deck therefore causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter, unless hero defeat has already ended the game. If only one card remains, draw it and take the exhaustion damage for the next missing draw.
- Played and resolved cards and discarded cards go into your own **face-up discard pile**, distinct from the face-down deck. Both players may inspect either discard pile **at any time**.
- Recovery cannot raise a fighter above their dial maximum. A later recovery effect cannot undo the immediate game end from hero defeat.
- “Move” follows paths and blockers; “place” puts the fighter directly in the permitted destination, with **one fighter per space** still required. Card permission to place anywhere is not limited to maneuver distance or a movement path.

1. **Declare** your attacking fighter (active fighter) and the opposing fighter targeted. Any fighter may attack an **adjacent** opponent, even across zone boundaries. **Melee** fighters may attack only adjacent opponents. **Ranged** fighters may also attack any opponent sharing a zone, regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part of that zone.
2. **Choose cards:** attacker plays an attack card face down that the attacking fighter is allowed to use. Defender may decline to play a card; otherwise plays a legal defense card face down for the defending fighter. **Reveal simultaneously** after both choices.
3. **Resolve combat** in the order below, then discard played cards to their owners’ **face-up discard piles**.

clauses: Full combat order
Priority for same-timing effects
Whether effects are optional
Other after-combat game effects
Played-card destination
answers.answer: Resolve immediately effects, during-combat effects, damage, after-combat card effects, other after-combat game effects, then discard all played cards to their owners’ face-up discard piles. Same-timing defender effect resolves first; effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise.

evidence.text:
1. Resolve **IMMEDIATELY** card effects.
2. Resolve **DURING COMBAT** card effects.
3. Determine combat result: defender takes attack value minus defense value, to a minimum of zero. If no defense card, take the attack value. Reduce the defending fighter’s health by the damage dealt. Defense does not itself deal return damage.
4. Resolve **AFTER COMBAT card effects**. A defeated fighter’s played card still resolves its after-combat effects **unless the game has already ended**.
5. Resolve other after-combat game effects, such as a hero’s special ability.
6. Finally place all played cards in their respective **face-up discard piles**.

**Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first.** Card effects are **mandatory unless they say otherwise** (for example “may”); this can harm your own fighters. Complete them in the printed order. A card whose effects are canceled keeps its printed combat value; the canceled effects do not resolve.

clauses: Given: attack 4 vs defense 4, then card effect deals 2 damage
Combat winner and reason
Attack damage with no defense against value 4
answers.answer: The defender wins combat because the attack itself dealt no damage; effect damage does not change the winner. With no defense card, attack damage is 4.

evidence.text: **Winning combat is not winning the game:** the attacker wins combat only if the **attack itself** deals at least 1 damage. If it deals none, the **defender wins**, including a tie of values or a defense that prevents the attack damage. Damage from effects does **not** change this winner.

clauses: Arthur and Merlin starting health
Their attack types and move value
When and how Arthur may BOOST an attack with his ability
Effect of cancellation on Arthur’s attack-card effects
answers.answer: The attached fighter reference and Arthur ability text answer these lookups.

evidence.text: | King Arthur | 18 | Melee | 2 | Merlin: 7, ranged |

**King Arthur:** Arthur and Merlin each use **move 2** during maneuver, before any BOOST. When **Arthur attacks**, he may BOOST the attack by playing a hand card **face down alongside his attack card**. Add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; the BOOST card is discarded. If the opponent **cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card**, this ability’s BOOST is **discarded without effect**. **Excalibur exception (official 2025 erratum):** Excalibur has no printed effects to cancel, so Feint does not remove the ability BOOST from a textless Excalibur attack. The BOOST still increases its attack value; the ordinary final discard of played cards still applies. See the sourced FAQ below. This is Arthur’s ability, not Merlin’s. **Noble Sacrifice** separately permits another BOOST during combat, in addition to the ability’s BOOST, if its effect is not canceled.

clauses: Sinbad and Porter health and attack types
Normal move value
Given three Voyages already in discard: maneuver distance for each fighter
Given three Voyages in discard: new base-2 Voyage combat value before other modifiers
Whether the played Voyage counts itself
answers.answer: With three Voyages in discard, each fighter’s maneuver allowance is 2 + 3 = 5 before any BOOST. A newly played Voyage has value 2 + 3 = 5 before other modifiers; it does not count itself because it is not yet in the discard pile. The attached reference supplies the requested stats.

evidence.text: | Sinbad | 15 | Melee | 2 | Porter: 6, melee |

**Sinbad:** when you maneuver, each of your fighters may move **+1 space for each VOYAGE card in your discard pile**, added to the normal move value 2 and any maneuver BOOST. The bonus also applies to Porter. The maneuver allowance is **2 + Voyages currently in discard + the chosen maneuver BOOST value**. Count the Voyages actually in the discard pile when moving: if Voyage Home is discarded to BOOST this maneuver, it counts in **both applicable terms**: +1 for being a Voyage in discard and +1 from its printed BOOST value.

All **7 Voyage** cards are **Sinbad-only attack cards, printed combat value 2, one copy each**. **Voyage Home has BOOST 1; the other six have no printed BOOST value.** Each has: **during combat, add 1 value for every Voyage card already in your discard pile**. Thus the normal value is **2 + that existing pile count**; exclude only the card currently being played because it is not in discard yet. **Three already-discarded Voyages give value 5.** Their separate after-combat effects are below; they **do not require winning** unless an effect explicitly says so.
